summary: Intermittent 503s observed on streaming sessions during high batch inference burst (dedicated pool, us-east)
description: Issue summary: Customers (NovaHealth Analytics) reported intermittent 503 responses when using streaming endpoints during a scheduled analytics batch run. Impact: Several streaming sessions terminated early; some requests returned 503 mid-stream. Scope: Limited to NovaHealth dedicated pool in us-east; observed on requests targeting rlhf-3b and open-llama-7b model variants. Timeline: 2026-03-11 11:38 UTC - first customer complaint in #support; 11:40 UTC - metrics show spike in request concurrency and drop in serving runtime successful responses; 11:45 UTC - automated alert: elevated 5xx rate on gateway; 11:50 UTC - mitigation: scaled nova-dedicated-pool by +2 instances; 12:10 UTC - partial reduction in 503s but not fully resolved. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use NovaHealth streaming integration to submit a burst of 1,000 concurrent streaming calls with average prompt length ~1k tokens; 2) Observe responses: a subset fails with 503 after initial chunk(s). Observed behavior: API Gateway returns 503 with error hint "upstream_reset" or "upstream_connection_closed" in gateway logs. Serving runtime logs show reaped worker processes around the same timestamps and transient OOM/kvcache evictions. Expected behavior: Streaming sessions should remain open for duration of inference or gracefully return 429/503 with retry guidance when overloaded. Temporary workaround applied: Reduced client concurrency and enabled conservative backoff on NovaHealth integration; we manually routed critical traffic to a warm spare capacity cluster. Next steps: SRE/Serving to continue investigation and implement hard caps and backpressure controls.
comments: 2026-03-11 11:42 UTC - Aisha P: Customer reporting 'chunk stream cut off mid-response' and 503s. Asked for request IDs and example timestamps.

2026-03-11 11:50 UTC - Danielle K (SRE): Observed gateway 5xx spike correlated with a surge in queued streaming connections. Note: upstream returned reset errors, investigating serving runtime process restarts.

2026-03-11 12:01 UTC - NovaHealth Support Rep (Elena): Confirmed they started a nightly analytics batch at 11:35 UTC that dramatically increased streaming concurrency; provided sample request-id: req_20260311_nova_7412.
2026-03-11 12:12 UTC - Danielle K: Scaled dedicated pool nova-dedicated-pool by +2 nodes, applied temporary gateway connection cap for NovaHealth route. 503 rate decreased ~60%.

2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - Jesse M (Serving Eng): Found multiple worker process restarts with high RSS near restart. Hypothesis: memory pressure during many concurrent streams causing eviction cascades and worker crashes leading gateway to surface 503s.
2026-03-12 11:27 UTC - Danielle K: Added conservative circuit-breaker policy to route (threshold lowered from 500 to 200 concurrent streams for this customer). Monitoring for week.
investigation_notes: Gateway logs (link): https://logs.redwood.ai/streaming/gateway/2026-03-11?query=req_20260311_nova_7412 - shows repeated 'upstream_connection_closed' and 'upstream_reset' entries at 11:40-11:55 UTC.
Serving runtime traces (link): https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/serving/2026-03-11 - several failed allocations and worker restarts on nodes nova-dedicated-03 and nova-dedicated-05.
Observability dashboard: 5xx-rate peaked at 18% for NovaHealth route; CPU and memory on affected nodes crossed 85% at peak. KV cache eviction rate spiked and correlated with restart times.
Heap/profile snapshot taken from nova-dedicated-05 at 11:49 UTC attached in attachments. Initial review shows sudden growth in transient per-request buffer allocations for streaming-chunk assembly.

Hypothesis 1: Concurrent streaming + long context prompts cause large per-request memory footprint; combined with unusual batching behavior triggers eviction and worker restarts -> gateway sees upstream dead connections -> 503.
Hypothesis 2: Gateway connection queue limit misconfiguration resulted in immediate 503s rather than queuing or returning 429; we should change policy to prefer graceful throttling.
Related PR being prepared to add per-route concurrency caps and a guardrail that returns 429 when route is over capacity instead of proxying to unhealthy upstream (see related_github_prs).
Linked incident: INC-20260311-CRIT (customer-impacting elevated 5xx) - postmortem scheduled after stability confirmed.
Affected customer CU contact: Elena Ruiz (NovaHealth) - engineering liaison provided sample logs and is testing suggested backoff settings.
Open action: replicate at scale in staging with synthetic streaming workload to reproduce memory growth pattern (assigned to Serving Eng).
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: scaled dedicated pool and applied temporary lower concurrency circuit-breaker for NovaHealth route which reduced 503 rate by ~60%. Customer asked to reduce concurrency while we implement permanent fixes. Planned remediation: (1) Implement per-route hard caps and graceful 429 responses in gateway (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/451), (2) add per-request streaming memory limits and allocation guards in serving-runtime to prevent worker restarts (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/792), (3) add automatic warm spare scaling for scheduled batch jobs on Dedicated. Follow-up: Post-incident review and runbook update to include guidance for large scheduled streaming batches. Status: In Progress - awaiting merged PRs and a controlled rollout.
